subject: Cleardata inference slate + benchlinks and next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@cleardata.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-08T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Cleardata inference slate + benchlinks and next steps

Thanks for the time today — great initial conversation on Cleardata's ingest and search augmentation use case. Quick recap + recommended next steps so we keep momentum.

Call recap (2-min):
- Goal: reduce query latency for search-surface expansions and cut per-query cost by ~40% while keeping high-answer accuracy for short (1-3 turn) assistant flows.
- Data: ~120M tokens/month, median query length 18 tokens, typical response target 80-250 tokens.
- Success metric: 95th-percentile latency < 250ms for single-turn queries and regression tolerance <= 3% on top-1 relevance MRR.

Recommended inference slate (initial pilot):
1) redwood/bison-8k-quant-v2 (hosted) — best latency vs quality for short-context retrieval-augmented prompts.
   - Verified profile (Redwood): 120 TPS, p50=12ms, p95=98ms, p99=160ms (8k context, 256 output tokens).
2) meta-llama-2-13b-q4a (dedicated trial) — stronger quality on long-form clarifications; higher cost but lower regression risk.
   - Verified profile: 22 TPS, p50=45ms, p95=210ms, p99=380ms (8k context, 256 output tokens).
3) openlm/mistral-7b-q8 (quantized) — low-cost fallback for bulk-batched summarization and analytics tasks.
   - Verified profile: 68 TPS, p50=18ms, p95=140ms, p99=260ms.

Benchmarks and artifacts shared:
- Redwood verified performance pack: https://console.redwood.ai/benchmarks/RDW-CLR-2026-07 (contains raw traces, kernel configs, and TPS/latency heatmaps)
- Prompt pack and initial evaluation prompts attached: prompt_set_for_cleardata_v3.txt
- Quick benchmark PDF with comparative cost estimates attached: cleardata_benchmarks_q3_v1.pdf

Quality/regression notes and guardrails:
- Recommendation: start with redwood/bison-8k-quant-v2 for the pilot and keep meta-llama-2-13b-q4a as a canary for queries flagged as high-risk (sensitive / legal / compliance).
- Set up automatic evals on a 200-sample prompt set (we included a starter set in the prompt pack). If top-1 MRR drops > 2.5% relative to initial baseline, auto-fallback to the canary model for that request class.
- Prefix/KV caching will provide 15–25% token cost savings for repeated contexts; see caching section in the drive link.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You share a 48–72 hour sample of query logs (anonymized) so we can run a quick calibration pass on the prompt pack.
2) We run a 2-week pilot (hosted + a 5-node dedicated trial for canary) and provide a TPS/latency dashboard and regression alerts.
3) Procurement: we can prepare an MSA + pilot SOW (I flagged procurement@cleardata.ai below).

Attaching the prompt pack and the short benchmark summary. Happy to jump back on a short call to walk through any of the profiles.

—
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0131

--- Attachments referenced: cleardata_benchmarks_q3_v1.pdf, prompt_set_for_cleardata_v3.txt
From: Olivia Grant <olivia@cleardata.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cleardata.ai
Date: 2026-09-08T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cleardata inference slate + benchlinks and next steps

Markus — thanks for the recap and the quick turnaround. A few clarifying items from our side after reading the materials: 

1) Tokenization / cost question: our request sizes are often 20–60 tokens in and 50–120 tokens out. The cost breakdown in the PDF looks optimistic for bison — can you confirm how you calculated the per-1k-token cost and whether the KV cache assumptions were applied?
2) Latency for multi-hop retrieval: when the pipeline does a triple-hop retrieval (retrieve -> re-rank -> final answer), does the TPS above assume batching across steps or per-request end-to-end time?
3) Procurement: what docs do you need to start the SOW? Our procurement team prefers an MSA with a compact pilot addendum; procurement@cleardata.ai pinged me the usual vendor forms.

Also — are there any sample prompt sets tuned specifically for high-precision retrieval answers (we saw the starter pack but want tuned variants)?

If you can answer these via email, procurement and I will triage. If a quick 20-min call tomorrow is easier, we can do that too.

Thanks,
Olivia
Head of Product, Cleardata Analytics
olivia@cleardata.ai
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-09T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Cleardata inference slate + benchlinks and next steps (internal notes)

Looping a couple of internal implementation notes for the pilot proposal — short bullets to include in the SOW and the pilot runbook: 

- Cost calc: redwood/bison-8k-quant-v2 numbers in the PDF include prefix caching at ~20% request reuse and continuous batching at 64-token average batch window; per-1k-token unit cost shown = hosted list *after discounts; we should show both gross and discounted numbers in the SOW.
- Triple-hop pipelines: the verified profiles are per-model p50/p95/p99 for single-generation calls. End-to-end triple-hop will require sequencing; recommend allowing a 10–20% added latency budget and instrumenting the call graph so we can attribute slow steps.
- Configs to test in pilot: (a) batching window 40–80ms, (b) KV cache TTL 30s for session reuse, (c) quant-enabled fallback route to mistral-7b for bulk post-processing.
- Telemetry: enable token-level tracing and the Redwood Console shared dashboard (we have view link).

I'll draft the SOW appendix language (pilot objectives, acceptance criteria, rollback triggers) and share a first pass by EOD tomorrow.

—Monica
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@cleardata.ai>, procurement@cleardata.ai
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-10T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cleardata inference slate + benchlinks and next steps

Thanks Olivia — answers inline below, plus a clear proposal for next week.

On tokenization / cost: the PDF shows the per-1k-token estimate after applying a 20% effective cache hit across your baseline workload and our standard PLG-hosted discounts for pilot customers. Raw hosted gross rates (no cache, list prices) are in the console link; we'll include a second table in the SOW that shows gross vs conservative vs optimistic cost bands so procurement can see both.

On triple-hop retrieval latency: the TPS/latency numbers are per-model generation. End-to-end: assume additive latencies for each model call plus retrieval/re-rank time. In practice we see triple-hop pipelines at ~1.6–2.1x single gen p95 depending on re-rank model size. We'll instrument this in the pilot and provide a call-graph view in the dashboard.

On tuned prompt sets: attached prompt_set_for_cleardata_v3.txt contains a tuned retrieval-precision variant (section B) and an auto-fallback trigger set (section C) for queries we want the canary model to handle. We'll also push a small suggested eval harness to the Drive folder for your team to run locally.

Proposed immediate actions: 
1) Cleardata: upload 48–72h anonymized query sample to the Drive folder (link above).
2) Redwood: Monica will send the pilot SOW appendix and the gross-vs-discounted cost table by EOD tomorrow.
3) Procurement: if you can share the standard vendor form + PO timeline, we will align legal and SAs to the pilot SOW.

Pilot timeline (suggested):
- Week 0: intake + sample ingest + smoke run (2–3 business days)
- Week 1: baseline runs vs recommended slate (hosted samples)
- Week 2: dedicated canary nodes + regression checks; handoff to Cleardata ops for validation

I've attached a simple pilot metric template (pilot_metric_template.csv) to collect MRR/latency/cost snapshots during the run. If that works, let's lock the kickoff for Sept 20 or Sept 22 — which works better for your team?

Best,
Markus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
